I am 64 years old, finished middle school, and have farmed for 40 years. My family has six people. My son and daughter-in-law work in a factory in Handan and send home about 3,000 yuan each month, so I have cash for inputs, but I still watch every yuan. I own 11.4 mu. Three mu I plant cotton, the other 8.4 mu I rotate wheat and maize. I have my own well with an electric pump.

It is early spring now. My wheat is already in the ground from last October. I rotary tilled before sowing and put down one 100-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu. Now the wheat is turning green. I will spread half a bag—50 jin—of urea per mu at green-up. At jointing stage I will irrigate, but I will not add more nitrogen. One bag of compound plus half a bag of urea is enough, and last year that gave me 540 kg per mu. In total that is 19 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphorus, and 7.5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times: the overwintering water I already did, then jointing water, and grain-filling water. I spray pesticide three times: herbicide once, then insecticide and fungicide. I expect 550 kg per mu this year.

For maize, after I harvest wheat in June, I will no-till plant hybrid maize right away. The summer season is short—only about 110 days—so I cannot waste time ploughing. I use 2.5 kg of hybrid seed per mu. I put one 100-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu in the row at sowing. At jointing I side-dress half a bag of urea per mu. That is 19 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphorus, and 7.5 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice: jointing and filling. I spray three times: herbicide at seedling stage, then two sprays for corn borer. I expect 600 kg per mu.

For cotton, I will plough the 3 mu in mid-April. I plant improved Bt cotton, 2 kg of seed per mu. Before planting I put one 100-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu plus 25 jin of potassium chloride per mu. Cotton needs more potassium or the bolls drop off. I topdress twice: at budding I spread 40 jin of urea per mu, at flowering another 10 jin. That is 19 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphorus, and 15 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times: budding, flowering, and boll-filling. I spray pesticide five times: even with Bt cotton, aphids, spider mites, and late bollworm still come. I target 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Where do these numbers come from? I copy what my neighbors do. Lao Zhang has good cotton, so I ask him how much he puts. I went to a village training meeting five years ago where they talked about balanced fertilizer, but I trust what I see in the field more. I would rather spend a little extra on fertilizer than risk losing yield. A bad harvest means I cannot pay for my grandson's school supplies; wasting some fertilizer is just money I could have saved. But I do think about my whole budget. If chemical fertilizer prices keep rising, I might cut back on the cotton area next year. For now, this is my plan. I have done this for 40 years. I know my land.
